source: MAFF Department of Agricultural Extension (នាយកដ្ឋានផ្សព្វផ្សាយកសិកម្ម), "បច្ចេកទេសដាំដុះសណ្តែកបាយ" (Mung Bean Cultivation Techniques handbook), Kingdom of Cambodia, MAFF, published by the Department of Agricultural Extension. Reference list on the closing page cites additional 2003-dated MAFF/agricultural-extension source booklets on mung bean varieties, seed production, and pest management, plus several international references (Plant Resources of South-East Asia Vol. I, 1992; Talekar & Skinner, Field Guide to Insect Pests of Tropical Asia, 1995; Nelson, Insect Pests of Vegetables, Philippines, 1969; Mung Bean Adaptation Trial, Kbalkoh Station 1996-2000, CLV Network; and a 1991 Bangkok workshop proceedings on Yellow Mosaic Virus). No elibrary.maff.gov.kh URL is visible on the scanned pages provided, so none is given here. Uploaded as a 38-page scanned PDF; no embedded text layer, all content read visually from page images. text: Black aphid (ខ្យងខ្មៅ, "Black Aphid"/black legume aphid, Aphis craccivora, family Aphididae, order Homoptera) reproduces asexually (parthenogenesis); individual body size is roughly 1.5-2 mm, sometimes with a waxy coating. Colonies form at the plant base and can expand rapidly, with the source giving a life-cycle length of roughly 2 weeks. Feeding damage occurs through sap-sucking from young shoots, causing stunted growth and leaf curl; this species is noted as capable of transmitting up to 14 different plant virus diseases. Prevention: scout fields before and after harvest to catch early populations; practice crop rotation rather than continuous mono-cropping; encourage natural predators such as ladybird beetles and hoverflies, which feed on aphids; farmers avoiding chemical pesticides can use a homemade garlic-and-chili extract spray, applied at early infestation and avoiding application during hot midday hours. Control: active ingredients named include Buprofezin, Acetamiprid, Thiamethoxam, and Deltamethrin, to be used following label directions for safe and effective use.
